utterances.text: Within the army, was there a military police?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: There was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did it also come under the mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Always, as part of a wartime unit. It's a simple platoon of a certain unit. There was never any separation between military conscript and military police conscripts. 2 Q. Yes, but within a unit, a military policeman had its own speciality, VES -

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, 11107. 4. Q. So according to the mobilisation, he would go to his unit and be a military policeman. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You mentioned Zeljko Meakic, and you said that you knew him well.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often would you see him in Omarksa?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Almost on a daily basis. Almost.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned somebody called Ranko Mijic.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, head of the crime section, known as Bajo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned several investigators, even those who interrogated you.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see Zeljko Meakic giving orders to Ranko Mijic and Bajo?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him issuing orders to other persons?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Which persons?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The investigators.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I never saw it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also mentioned Mr. Kvocka.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified that you knew him extremely well from the building you worked in?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Not extremely well and not personally, but I did know him. I said "not personally."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry then. Mr. Keegan mentioned the process of identification and that in your conversations with the investigators, you were asked to carry out certain identifications on a photo board, and you recognised many people there; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Many persons from the "glass house," yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that identification procedure, was any kind of pressure brought to bear on you?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: When the -- are you talking about this photograph? This is the photograph I saw in Germany, on television.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I'm talking about the identification for the investigators.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no pressure was brought to bear on me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they explain to you the procedure of identification?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you tell them that you had understood the procedure?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Keegan mentioned three photo boards being shown to you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher to show you, please, this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Keegan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEEGAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've been through this procedure a number of times now, and I didn't introduce the reports because it had already been indicated to me prior to the hearing today that they intended to introduce them. Mr. Simic would be well aware that the witness doesn't see the report, so the witness can't identify the report at all. The witness is given instructions. They're not told who they're looking for at all, they're simply shown a photo board and asked if they can recognise anybody. Then the results are recorded by an investigator in a report, who signs that report. Now, we have no objection to the report coming in, and we have no objection to the photo board coming in, of course, but we do object to Mr. Simic continually trying to get witnesses to somehow make comment on documents which they've never seen. If I could just continue for one second, Your Honour. From the look of confusion that I think I see, the only thing Mr. Mesanovic would have seen was the photo board, and he would have been asked to sign certain photo boards, but the actual report that is signed by the investigator he would not be shown, and that's what I'm talking about. So I have no objection to any of the documents be entered, it's what's shown to the witness personally, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you understood Mr. Keegan's observation, and do you have anything to say in response, Mr. Simic? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Yes, I have understood Mr. Keegan's observation. Those observations are partially well founded, but I will put the questions to the witness which the investigator put to Mr. Mesanovic. There is no need for me to show him this. I just wanted to speed up the proceedings. All he needs to do is to see the photo board. I thought we would save time in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the witness knows well the photographs. He has seen them. Maybe to speed things up you could simply ask the questions that you wanted to ask the witness, except if you have a very particular point regarding a particular photograph or a specific detail. This is always the issue that we have discussed from the beginning. We have always discussed the use of such documents. The majority of Defence counsel upheld the opinion that what counted, what is the most important, is what happens here. And that the statements would only be used to put questions but not to repeat things, not to show them to the witness. Do you remember that, Mr. Krstan Simic? We are using documents that you know. You can use them to put the questions that you have. You will remember that we had a very lengthy discussion that we had here, and I remember Defence counsel saying, "We will take the statement, and we'll proceed." Others said that the principle of orality is what counts. What the witness says here is important, even for the cross-examination. Therefore, proceed with your questions. Please proceed, Mr. Krstan Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Could I ask the usher to give this photo board to Mr. Mesanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krstan Simic, one other question. How much time do you need to finish with the cross-examination? Because it is already 2.30. It is past 2.30. How much time do you need? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Two or three questions. I am close at the end of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then. Please continue, Mr. Krstan Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, was this photo board shown to you during the identification procedure?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: There were so many boards that I simply don't remember whether I saw this or not. I don't remember. Maybe it was one of the photo boards that was shown to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you look at it now, please? Let me repeat the questions put to you at the time by a representative of the Office of the Prosecutor. Did you recognise any person on that photo board linked to crimes committed within the territory of Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I recognise Zigic. About -- I think in the right-hand corner there is Kvocka, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you take a close look, please?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: He looks like it but I can't guarantee. I think it is him but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, was this photo board shown to you at all?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't remember. It was a long time ago. Regarding this particular photo board, what is there in it that would make me remember this particular one? I told you that I didn't recognise anyone. But there was a dozen photo also boards, with moustaches, without moustaches, with a beard, without a beard.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But linked to this photo board, according to the report of the investigator, he asked you the following question: "Do you find a photograph among these photographs of somebody that you know for any reason at all?"

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Finally no. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. We have no further questions. We would like to tender the report of the investigator as our Exhibit number 32, as well as this photo board which, according to the Prosecution, was shown to Mr. Mesanovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mesanovic, I have no further questions. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you too, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Madam Registrar, what would be the exhibit number for this document, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: May I have the document first? We always need a copy of the document so that we can take a look at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just the photo board.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: D32/1. Sorry. D32/1. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the end of the testimony, we will review the admission of several exhibits used either by the Prosecution or the Defence. For today, we will stop there. Witness, you will have to come back tomorrow to continue the cross-examination. That will be all for today, and the usher will see you out. We will see you again tomorrow at 9.30.
